content.title: Review export popover defaults before queuing an export
content.intent: Prove the export popover presents the complete action list, shared action chrome, complete format list, and CSV as the initial selected format before any export is queued.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to review the complete set of action titles and format titles as one initial-state path because the source defined finite discrete options. Applied rendered-surface inspection for shared chrome because the source promised icon and description on each action. Skipped boundary value analysis, negative/error, state/flow, auth, i18n, responsiveness, persistence, and pagination because the source stated no constrained input, failure path, gated role, locale behavior, alternate viewport behavior, refresh behavior, or collection semantics. No covering array was needed because this scenario inspected the initial state rather than a combination matrix. Estimated total design size remained 4 scenario/test pairs, below budget ceiling 8.

content.title: Queue CSV exports from each export action
content.intent: Prove each export action can be queued while the default CSV format remains selected and a success toast is shown.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning across the four export actions because they are discrete choices with the same promised visible outcome. Used covering-array authority over input classes {action}; requested strength 2 from the user-reach-only risk profile and accepted the tool's degradation to strength 1 because only one varying input remained once the format stayed at the default CSV value. Skipped boundary, negative, state-flow, auth, persistence, i18n, a11y, responsiveness, and pagination techniques because the source defined no invalid action, multi-step gate, stored side effect, locale rule, accessibility promise, viewport rule, or sortable/filterable list behavior. Estimated total design size remained 4 scenario/test pairs, below budget ceiling 8.

content.title: Queue JSON exports from each export action
content.intent: Prove the export format can be changed from the default to JSON before queuing any export action and a success toast is shown.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning across the four export actions with the JSON format fixed, because the source promised the same success-feedback outcome regardless of which export action is chosen. Used covering-array authority over input classes {action}; requested strength 2 from the user-reach-only risk profile and accepted the tool's degradation to strength 1 because only one varying input remained after fixing format to JSON. Kept this separate from the CSV path because changing away from the default creates a distinct journey that must prove the non-default format can be selected before export. Skipped boundary, negative, state-flow, auth, persistence, i18n, a11y, responsiveness, and pagination for the same evidence-based reasons as the CSV path. Estimated total design size remained 4 scenario/test pairs, below budget ceiling 8.

content.title: Queue PDF exports from each export action
content.intent: Prove the export format can be changed from the default to PDF before queuing any export action and a success toast is shown.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning across the four export actions with the PDF format fixed, because the source promised the same success-feedback outcome regardless of the chosen export action. Used covering-array authority over input classes {action}; requested strength 2 from the user-reach-only risk profile and accepted the tool's degradation to strength 1 because only one varying input remained after fixing format to PDF. Kept this separate from the CSV path because changing away from the default creates a distinct journey that must prove the non-default format can be selected before export. Skipped boundary, negative, state-flow, auth, persistence, i18n, a11y, responsiveness, and pagination for the same evidence-based reasons as the other export paths. Estimated total design size remained 4 scenario/test pairs, below budget ceiling 8.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applicable because the source defines finite discrete export actions and format options that can be partitioned into representative user-visible choices.
[applicability] Not applicable because the export popover exposes no numeric, ordered, or length-bounded input in the cited evidence.
[applicability] Not applicable because the cited source states no invalid input, blocked action, or error-handling behavior for this popover.
[applicability] Not applicable because the described interaction is a short choose-and-queue action, not a multi-step stateful flow with gated transitions.
[applicability] Not applicable because the source does not promise creation, persistence, update, deletion, or durable record mutation; it explicitly says no real export is necessary.
[applicability] Not applicable because no login gate, role rule, or permission distinction appears in the use-case or cited source lines.
[applicability] Not applicable because the promised behavior is a UI popover interaction, not a REST or GraphQL surface.
[applicability] Not applicable because the cited export behavior does not involve shared-resource mutation, money movement, or race-sensitive state.
[applicability] Not applicable because the source promises only fake success feedback and no durable write effect that a retry could duplicate.
[applicability] Not applicable because the cited export popover text does not promise locale-dependent rendering or formatting behavior.
[applicability] Not applicable for scenario expansion because the source contains no accessibility-specific promise to turn into a distinct path.
[applicability] Not applicable because the source gives a fixed popover width but no alternate viewport or layout adaptation rule.
[applicability] Not applicable because the popover is an option chooser, not a list or search result surface with a zero-results condition.
[applicability] Not applicable because no numeric quantity or bounded counter is present in the cited export interaction.
[applicability] Not applicable because the source does not state refresh, relaunch, or resume behavior for export selection state.
[applicability] Not applicable because the cited export behavior mentions no schedule, TTL, or time-based transition.
[applicability] Not applicable because the export popover promises labels, choices, and feedback, not currency rendering or rounding.
[applicability] Not applicable because the export popover is not a searchable or paginated collection surface.
[applicability] Not applicable because the popover does not upload or manage media; it only queues export actions.
[applicability] Not applicable because the only promised effect is an in-page success toast, not an out-of-band notification or async channel.
